hard_case: Spec example 4: `facade` has `pub use inner::*;` and an `Ext` trait; its integration test has `use facade::*;` and calls only `v.go(3)`, so the facade-package test may reach the changed owner through the re-export but never names it.

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: bump_counter(&mut v, 3) turns 2 instead of 1, but `Ext::go` pushes and counts by itself and never calls it

reasoning: `facade/tests/t.rs` pins `v.go(3)`, but `Ext::go` for `Vec<u8>` does not call `inner::bump_counter`, so no mutant of it can fail. The test never names the owner and the facade re-exports it, so ripr names the untraced path (`no_static_path` with `rust_integration_public_api_path_unresolved`) and stays non-actionable instead of reading a definite absence. Spec cells: RIPR-SPEC-0118 example 4.
